promotionRule: No route in Batch 074 is eligible for generation or promotion. All six remain asset-free scientific-media holds until the named article corrections are committed and independently re-audited.

routeDecisions.reason: The page conflates transfer processes with genetic vehicles and universalizes co-selection, intI1, persistence, diet, and biofilm claims beyond the cited evidence.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Separate identities and mechanisms; evidence-grade linkage and environmental claims; source the biofilm section; and bound the small diet comparison before re-audit.

routeDecisions.reason: The heterogeneous HMO family lacks an exact controlled identifier and the page contains obsolete formula claims, teleology, absolutes, and unbounded NEC and microbiome causation.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define family scope, update formula supplementation, separate evidence tiers, remove absolutes, and bound structure-, strain-, product-, and population-specific findings.

routeDecisions.reason: The page collapses H2S/HS− speciation, understates microbial production routes, relies on a protocol for disease claims, and overgeneralizes dose, diet, metal, and disease effects.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Separate chemical species and donors, cover major microbial routes, replace mis-scoped citations, and bound all tissue-, dose-, assay-, and model-specific effects.

routeDecisions.reason: A generic family title is used for a pathogen-focused [NiFe] thesis with malformed source keys and unsupported saturation, nickel, virulence, cancer, diet, and therapeutic extrapolations.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Choose a general or narrow scope, normalize source keys, map claims to primary organism/model evidence, and remove unsupported clinical and dietary causation.

routeDecisions.reason: The definition is nonstandard and the page misclassifies ordinary food crops as botanical hyperaccumulators while asserting an unsupported microbiome-disease chain.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Use element-specific ecological criteria, separate true hyperaccumulators from crop contaminant accumulation, and remove the unsupported causal chain.

routeDecisions.reason: The page falsely calls aromatase zinc-dependent, stores the trace-element study under an unrelated DOI, and overstates heterogeneous PCOS microbiome associations as central mechanisms and treatment targets.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Remove the false zinc-aromatase chain, correct DOI and author metadata, rebuild trace-element outcomes, distinguish PCOS from hyperandrogenism, and evidence-grade microbiome and treatment claims.
